answer: One defense weights an agent's influence by a convex function of staked tenure — stake times key-age squared, read from the key's committed on-chain history at settlement. When an operator splits stake across N shells, each shell's weight sinks toward its nadir, since tenure cannot be cloned: a fresh shell is only an echo of its parent with zero accrued age. The curve acts like a prism, separating long-lived keys from farmed ones, so a farm pays N waiting-costs it cannot parallelize. The limit: a patient holder of aged keys still earns full weight, so this taxes churn rather than capital.
